scope: Targeted primary-source selection; not an exhaustive or thousand-paper full-text review.

sources.title: On the Kinematics of Wheeled Mobile Robots
sources.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research 8(5), 15–27
sources.supports: Planar wheel compatibility and coordinated steering/drive rates; wheel misalignment can cause slip.
sources.read_depth: Publisher abstract and institutional manuscript introduction.
sources.caution: Ideal rolling assumptions do not certify rough-terrain traction or independently steerable hardware.

sources.title: Kinematics, dynamics and control design of 4WIS4WID mobile robots
sources.supports: Four steering and four drive actuators require coordinated control; kinematic and dynamic tracking architecture.
sources.read_depth: Publisher abstract, introduction and section listing.
sources.caution: Reported verification is simulation; neither controller performance nor steering range transfers to Nemesis.
sources.license: CC BY 3.0 stated on publisher page.

sources.title: Kinematic control design for wheeled mobile robots with longitudinal and lateral slip
sources.venue: International Journal of Adaptive Control and Signal Processing
sources.supports: Slip requires explicit modeling/adaptation; longitudinal and lateral disturbances have different control consequences.
sources.read_depth: Author arXiv abstract, metadata and linked journal reference.
sources.caution: Nonholonomic model and numerical simulations; cannot claim observed Nemesis slip compensation.

sources.title: A New Measure of Tipover Stability Margin for Mobile Manipulators
sources.venue: Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation, 3111–3116
sources.supports: Force-angle stability metric accounts for top-heaviness, external/inertial loads and uneven contact geometry.
sources.caution: Do not reduce dynamic tipover certification to COM projection alone; requires masses, contact points and loads.

sources.title: Unified motion control of 4WIS-4WID WMR with unlimited steering and load transfer consideration
sources.supports: Recent example of force allocation including slip, friction constraints and load transfer.
sources.caution: Unlimited steering is an explicit hardware assumption; Nemesis cable routing and servo limits preclude assuming it.

sources.title: Traction Control of Wheeled Robotic Vehicles in Rough Terrain with Application to Planetary Rovers
sources.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research 23(10–11), 1029–1040
sources.supports: Terrain/contact-aware wheel torque allocation, redundant actuation and traction/power objectives.
sources.read_depth: Publisher abstract and author laboratory publication record.
sources.caution: Needs terrain/contact estimates and suitable feedback; simple friction-cap calculations are only screening bounds.

sources.title: On-Line Terrain Parameter Estimation for Planetary Rovers
sources.venue: Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation 3, 3142–3147
sources.supports: Onboard terrain identification links rover measurements to traversability and traction prediction.
sources.caution: Loose-sand results depend on sensors and soil models; do not borrow parameters for the photographed tires.

sources.title: Optimal Rough Terrain Trajectory Generation for Wheeled Mobile Robots
sources.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research 26(2), 141–166
sources.supports: Forward-model trajectory optimization can include propulsion, suspension, wheel-terrain interaction and constraints.
sources.read_depth: Author institutional abstract and manuscript abstract.
sources.caution: A rendered route is not an optimization result; calibrated forward models are required.

sources.title: The Dynamic Window Approach to Collision Avoidance
sources.supports: Local collision avoidance should respect feasible velocity/acceleration and braking constraints.
sources.read_depth: Author institutional publication record and indexed abstract.
sources.caution: Original synchro-drive setting; 4WIS steering rate and footprint constraints need a custom feasible-command layer.

sources.title: Real-Time Obstacle Avoidance for Manipulators and Mobile Robots
sources.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research 5(1), 90–98
sources.supports: Artificial potential fields and operational-space obstacle avoidance provide a classical baseline.
sources.read_depth: Publisher abstract and author-hosted PDF indexed introduction.
sources.caution: A local reactive field does not by itself establish globally complete or deadlock-free navigation.

sources.title: ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual–Inertial, and Multimap SLAM
sources.supports: Candidate high-level visual-inertial localization stack with calibrated cameras, IMU and map reuse.
sources.read_depth: Publisher abstract/introduction and author preprint abstract.
sources.caution: Compute, calibration and sensor requirements are additional to Mega/ESP32; benchmark errors are not Nemesis accuracy.

sources.title: RTAB-Map as an open-source lidar and visual simultaneous localization and mapping library for large-scale and long-term online operation
sources.supports: Practical lidar/visual SLAM alternatives and resource-aware long-term map management.
sources.read_depth: Official project bibliography and author-uploaded abstract.
sources.caution: ArXiv upload 2024 is not journal publication year; choose one stack experimentally rather than claim both implemented.

sources.title: Sampling-based Algorithms for Optimal Motion Planning
sources.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research 30(7), 846–894
sources.supports: RRT*/PRM* establish an asymptotically optimal planning baseline under stated assumptions.
sources.caution: Asymptotic optimality does not guarantee a finite-time optimal, executable rover route.

sources.title: The Open Motion Planning Library
sources.supports: Reusable sampling-based planning library for future arm/base planning and reproducible baselines.
sources.read_depth: Author laboratory publication page and abstract.
sources.caution: Collision geometry, limits and validity checking remain application responsibilities.

sources.title: Comprehensive Standard Test Suites for the Performance Evaluation of Mobile Robots
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 2010 Performance Metrics for Intelligent Systems Workshop
sources.supports: Repeatable mobility, sensing, communication, manipulation, energy and interface evaluation.
sources.caution: Proposed use of test methods is not certification or proof of standards compliance.

sources.title: Performance of Emergency Response Robots
authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.venue: NIST program page; updated 24 April 2026; accessed 15 September 2026
sources.supports: Current task-based test framework and distinction between test methods and mission-specific pass thresholds.
sources.read_depth: Official page objectives, test categories and standard listing.
sources.caution: Use as validation-plan source; don't label a visual concept mission-capable without repeatable tests.

sources.title: Design and implementation of a maxi-sized mobile robot (Karo) for rescue missions
sources.supports: Integrated rescue platform comparison; modular mechanical design, manipulator workspace, actuator sizing and structured evaluation.
sources.read_depth: Publisher full-text sections: conceptual/mechanical design, torque, manipulation, figure captions and rights. Correction also checked.
sources.caution: Tracked four-flipper platform differs fundamentally from Nemesis; don't transplant dimensional results. Arm torque paragraph has apparent numerical/notation inconsistencies, so independently recompute.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0; third-party exclusions apply; Figures 6 and 9 have no separate excluded credit in inspected captions.

sources.title: ResQbot 2.0: An Improved Design of a Mobile Rescue Robot with an Inflatable Neck Securing Device for Safe Casualty Extraction
sources.supports: Comparison showing physical rescue intervention requires dedicated mechanisms and a separate safety validation program.
sources.read_depth: Publisher sections/abstract; original PDF license, figure 10 photo, abstract and conclusion context.
sources.caution: Reported casualty-extraction validation is simulation. Nemesis has no supplied patient transport capability; use comparison, not feature transfer.

sources.title: Development of a Four Omni-Wheeled Mobile Robot Using Telescopic Legs
sources.supports: Comparable low-cost controller integration and explicit 3D-to-prototype documentation; active leg design versus fixed rover architecture.
sources.read_depth: Publisher full-text/PDF system-design, kinematic sections, Figure 1 and license.
sources.caution: Omni-wheel and telescopic-leg kinematics do not apply to Nemesis conventional tires; no inferred stair-climbing claim.
